`write_manual()` generates copy-pasteable base R code that reproduces a powerrules calculation using the paper's constants (2.5 for 80% power, 3.3 for 95% power, 1.64 for the critical value with 90% CIs).
This lets researchers verify the computation without any dependencies beyond base R.

## Running the pipeline

Suppose we plan to replicate @Ahler2018, who find that correcting respondents' misperceptions of their out-party reduces affective polarization.
The standard deviation of feeling thermometer responses in the 2020 ANES is 20.8.
We plan to recruit 500 respondents per condition and assume a treatment effect of 3 points (the lower bound of Ahler and Sood's 95% confidence interval).

```{r}
library(powerrules)

result <- from_sd(sd_y = 20.8) |>
  find_power(n = 500, tau = 3)
```

## Generating the manual calculation code

`write_manual()` takes the result and prints a self-contained base R script:

```{r}
write_manual(result)
```

## Running the generated code

The generated code computes the predicted SE and power using base R only.
The result matches the analytical 74% from powerrules.

```{r}
# Manual power calculation

# --- Inputs ---
sd_y <- 20.8   # SD of outcome in reference population
n    <- 500    # respondents per condition
tau  <- 3      # assumed treatment effect

# --- Predicted SE (Rule 3) ---
se <- 2 * sd_y / sqrt(2 * n)

# --- Power (Rule 2) ---
power <- 1 - pnorm(1.64 - tau / se)

cat("Predicted SE:        ", round(se, 2), "\n")
cat("tau / SE:            ", round(tau / se, 2), "\n")
cat("Power:               ", round(power * 100), "%\n")
```
